title: Grateful Dead Live at O'Keefe Centre on 1967-08-04
source: Stereo SBD MR>R>DAT(3)>CDR(unknown number of CD gens)>EAC> Cool Edit 2000>CD Wave>SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a 1967 show with strong Viola Lee and New Potato performances, though the tape runs slightly fast.
ai_review.review: The recording showcases an early‑stage Dead jam where Jerry Garcia and Phil Lesh weave improvisational counterpoint on "Viola Lee," ending in one of the first extended feedback passages that would later become the band’s famed “space.”  Both "Viola Lee" and "New Potato" are highlighted as high‑energy moments, but listeners note that the tape runs a bit fast, requiring pitch correction for optimal playback.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews consistently rate 4–5 stars and praise the musical performance; only a modest technical flaw (speed issue) tempers the overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Tape runs fast, causing pitch/speed distortion; otherwise clear enough for listeners to enjoy after correction. No major drop‑outs or muffling reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Improvised counterpoint between Jerry and Phil builds into a pioneering feedback outro that was cut off on this release, giving the show an experimental edge.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his improvisational work and tone during "Viola Lee"; central to the early feedback experiment.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted as a key part of the improvised counterpoint with Jerry up through about 1975.
